small_guidance:
- The current conv_mean kernel iterates IC×KD×KH×KW with scalar loads per (oc,hw) — replace inner gather with a GEMM-style tile: load a [BLOCK_OC, IC] weight slab and a [IC, BLOCK_HW] input slab per (kd,kh,kw,od) and use tl.dot to accumulate. Start BLOCK_HW=64, BLOCK_OC=32, and add an autotune sweep over (BLOCK_HW∈{64,128}, BLOCK_OC∈{32,64}, num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}).
- Swap loop order so od is innermost (or fold it into kd): for stride=1, depth output OD≈D+KD-1 with most kd contributing only once per od; precompute valid (od,kd,id) pairs and skip the per-od redundancy by accumulating across od inline (sum over od of x[id]) before multiplying by w[kd], cutting the KD factor in the spatial loops.
- Make IC the GEMM-K axis with channels-first contiguous weight reshaped to [IC, OC*KD*KH*KW] and use tl.dot; this alone should remove most of the 4× gap to baseline.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style implicit GEMM where each program computes a tile of (OC, OH*OW) for one (n, od_block) and the K-loop walks IC*KD*KH*KW with tl.dot. Fuse the depth-mean by accumulating across all OD inside the same program (one persistent tile per (n, oh_tile, oc_tile)) and divide by OD in the epilogue — this removes the OD-fold redundancy and turns the kernel into a single fused conv-transpose+mean GEMM.
- Since stride=1 and KD=KH=KW=3, ConvTranspose3d is equivalent to Conv3d with the weight flipped and padding=KD-1-pad; pre-flip the weight once at init (this is a layout transform, not a reduction) and run a standard Conv3d-style implicit GEMM. Then fuse +bias, softmax-over-channels, tanh, scale into the same kernel's epilogue when the OC tile equals OC (persist OC in registers per (n,oh,ow)).
- Use channels_last memory layout for x and out so the IC/OC axis is contiguous, enabling vectorized 128-bit loads in the GEMM-K dimension; this is the biggest single-bandwidth win on a 4090.
